rulings.challenge_claim: The span closes on a doubled ketiv/qere verse (MT 22:23) with no variant disclosure anywhere in the row and an unqualified span-wide null asserted in its place, and the two notes sit on the very feminine-singular forms the addressee-shift warrant rests on.
rulings.grounds: The variant layer is byte-confirmed and the omission is real. Two ketiv/qere notes stand at oshb:Jer.22.23 - a member of the twelve doubled-note verses - and both pairs sit inline in the source bytes, unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere: ישבתי יֹשַׁבְתְּ֙ and מקננתי מְקֻנַּ֖נְתְּ (oshb:Jer.22.23, byte tier). The parashah half of the disclosure is exact: a setumah closes oshb:Jer.22.19 and no petuchah or setumah falls in Jer.22.20-Jer.22.23 (single-witness, tier-3 weak). But device_notes then states that no mark falls within the span without naming the layer that statement is true of, over the row's own closing verse, in the book's largest variant inventory. The declared false-positive disposition against that finding fails on its own terms: the verse is inside the span, not adjacent to it, and the notes are two, not one. Where the filed framing overshoots is reach. The stated ground is a feminine-singular address, and both readings in each pair carry that same address - the unpointed forms differ from the pointed ones in the archaic final yod, not in the person addressed - so the variants corroborate the warrant instead of contesting it, and the address is independently byte-visible across the span in זֶ֤ה דַרְכֵּךְ֙ מִנְּעוּרַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Jer.22.21, byte tier) and מִכֹּ֖ל רָעָתֵֽךְ (oshb:Jer.22.22, byte tier). The English quoted as closing evidence, “Inhabitant of Lebanon, who makes your nest in the cedars” (web:Jer.22.23), renders a sense both readings support, which is why quote coverage triggers the disclosure duty even though nothing in the rendering turns on the choice - and why the contrary position, that no disclosure is owed because only the English of that verse is cited, does not hold: the span-relevant disclosure duty is unconditional, not quote-conditional. The seam is untouched: עֲלִ֤י הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ וּֽצְעָ֔קִי (oshb:Jer.22.20, byte tier) carries no variant note. Corrected finding: a disclosure and clarity defect at medium, not a warrant defect at high.
rulings.remedy: In device_notes, qualify the null to the layer it is true of (no petuchah or setumah falls within Jer.22.20-Jer.22.23) and add the variant disclosure: two ketiv/qere notes at oshb:Jer.22.23 (WLC, single-witness), a doubled-note verse, unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere in each pair, with one clause stating that both readings carry the same feminine-singular address so the addressee ground is unaffected. Leave span, confidence, unit_type and observed_substrate_signals unchanged. The cure must pass the test that killed the original: the quote-coverage arm over ketiv/qere verses - an English quotation covering a variant-bearing verse must carry a ketiv/qere disclosure - returns clean, and a span-relevant disclosure sweep over Jer.22.20-Jer.22.23 names every layer (parashah none in span, paseq none, special letters none, ketiv/qere two at 22:23).

rulings.challenge_claim: The single-unit reading is argued in a device vocabulary that cannot register the recurrent macro-onset formula standing twice inside the span - verse-initially at MT 23:5 and in its lachen shape at MT 23:7, each immediately after a setumah the row itself discloses - while the rejected alternative tests a split point with no such support.
rulings.grounds: Every arm verifies on the bytes. הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה opens oshb:Jer.23.5 verse-initially and לָכֵ֛ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה opens oshb:Jer.23.7 (both byte tier). The object is book-wide rather than local colour: the three-word announcement run stands in 15 verses (sweep: 15 verses, MT keys), 14 of them verse-initial - 6 bare and 8 lachen-prefixed - the single non-initial member carrying a ki prefix at oshb:Jer.30.3, and one member falling inside the renumbering zone (oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25). Both in-span onsets fall immediately after the two setumahs device_notes already names, so the substrate layer and the formula layer coincide at the same two joins, while the cohesion test is worded as the absence of an addressee, scene or discourse-imperative seam - a vocabulary in which neither join can appear. The closing pair is itself a recurring block: oshb:Jer.23.7-Jer.23.8 shares with oshb:Jer.16.14-Jer.16.15 an identical seven-word consonantal opening and, after the one divergent verb form, an identical sixteen-word consonantal run (skeleton tier), which argues that the pair carries its own header rather than terminating one sustained speech, and that goes undisclosed. Tier discipline holds the finding to the warrant: the announcement formula is a tier-1 text signal but is not among the internal-cut classes the granularity rule licenses, so nothing here decides a seam - whether a recurrent announcement onset can close a unit against the postpositive divine formula standing inside it is left open, and any cut at 23:4|23:5 or 23:6|23:7 remains a boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption, never author work. Two findings beyond the challenge. First, the tested rival is not signal-free: the direct second-person address to the shepherds, אַתֶּ֞ם הֲפִצֹתֶ֤ם אֶת צֹאנִי֙ (oshb:Jer.23.2, byte tier), is not carried past that join - וַאֲנִ֗י אֲקַבֵּץ֙ (oshb:Jer.23.3, byte tier) opens unaddressed divine first-person speech, and 23:4-23:8 speak of shepherds and flock in the third person - so the flat denial that any addressee seam marks the turn is contestable on the row's own criterion, while what the join genuinely lacks is the announcement onset and any parashah mark. Second, one paseq seg stands at oshb:Jer.23.6 inside the span (count-only, WLC single-witness) and is undisclosed. The residual on the 23:6 name is real but low: an onomastic label is applied with no pointed splice, though no digit rests on it.
rulings.remedy: (1) device_notes: add the one paseq seg at oshb:Jer.23.6 (count-only, single-witness, no intra-verse position claim) beside the setumahs already named; disclose both in-span announcement onsets with pointed splices bound to oshb:Jer.23.5 and oshb:Jer.23.7 at byte tier, naming the swept object and its digit in the sanctioned shorthand (sweep: 15 verses, MT keys) and writing the zone member dually (oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25) if the set is enumerated; disclose the closing pair's near-twin at oshb:Jer.16.14-Jer.16.15 at skeleton tier as cross-seam texture, explicitly not a boundary driver. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut so the tested join is described by the signals it carries and lacks - the second-person address to the shepherds ends there, while no announcement onset and no parashah mark stands - replacing the unqualified no-addressee denial; one sentence plus at most the mandated rival-disclosure sentence. (3) Either splice the pointed name at oshb:Jer.23.6 with its tier or drop the onomastic label. (4) Span, unit_type and confidence unchanged; no boundary change is author work. Tests the cure must pass: a span-relevant disclosure sweep over Jer.23.1-Jer.23.8 names parashah, paseq and ketiv/qere; every device argued in prose carries a byte-tier splice bound to its cited ref and every digit names its swept object and unit; and the re-cut rejected alternative survives a byte re-read of the join it names - the read the original failed.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both items strike the same sentence: the rejected alternative grounds cohesion on 23:13-23:14 continuing the same first-person indictment opened at 23:9, but 23:9 carries the prophet's own non-indicting distress and the indicting first person is the divine speaker's, not established until 23:11; the second item adds that this speaker change meets the row's own opening-seam criterion at a point inside the span it never engages.
rulings.grounds: Same defect at core, with the second item adding a distinct arm; both hold on the bytes. At oshb:Jer.23.9 the first person is the prophet's and accuses no one - נִשְׁבַּ֧ר לִבִּ֣י בְקִרְבִּ֗י - with the divine name standing in the third person in that same verse, מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה (both byte tier); that is precisely the ground boundary_rationale uses to open the unit. From oshb:Jer.23.11 the first person is the divine speaker's, גַּם בְּבֵיתִ֛י מָצָ֥אתִי רָעָתָ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte tier), with the postpositive formula closing 23:12 as well, and that voice carries רָאִ֣יתִי תִפְלָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.23.13, byte tier) into the sentence at 23:15. The rejected alternative's predicate is therefore false on the bytes and inconsistent with the row's own opening account - a blended speech-role claim of exactly the class the frame-ownership discipline forbids, where the mouth is named at the seam and then left unnamed across the body. The second arm is a genuine disclosure gap: the voice change treated as seam-worthy at the opening recurs inside the span and is never named. It does not, however, open a rival seam - oshb:Jer.23.11 opens כִּֽי גַם (byte tier), a ki-subordinated clause continuing the ground of 23:10, and no tier-1 onset device stands at that join - so cohesion holds and the cut itself is not in doubt. On the disclosure layers nothing further is owed: the marks disclosed over the span are correct under type (setumah at 23:13 and 23:14, petuchah at 23:15, single-witness, tier-3 weak) and no ketiv/qere note or paseq seg falls in Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the ground so it names the mouth at each first person - the opening distress at Jer.23.9 is the prophet's, with the divine speaker in the third person there, while the indicting first person runs from Jer.23.11 through the sentence at Jer.23.15 - and rest the cohesion on the ki-subordination at Jer.23.11 and on the sentence that 23:13-23:14 feeds, not on one continuous voice. Keep to one sentence plus at most the mandated rival-disclosure sentence; span, unit_type, confidence and observed_substrate_signals unchanged. Tests the cure must pass: every first-person claim in the field names whose mouth carries it, and the re-cut sentence survives the byte read of oshb:Jer.23.9 and oshb:Jer.23.11 that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's own splice shows the opening verse is carried by a verse-initial koh-amar-tsevaot frame, yet the opener is labelled a discourse-frame imperative, the mouth carrying the formula is never named, and the frame is absent from the declared signals - while the rejected alternative excuses the following seam for lacking exactly that marker.
rulings.grounds: Verified at every point. oshb:Jer.23.16 opens verse-initially on כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת (byte tier); the imperative the rationale names, אַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ (byte tier), stands after it, not at the verse head. The splice filed in boundary_rationale contains the whole run including the frame, yet the opener is described only as a discourse-frame imperative and observed_substrate_signals records only the imperative and the addressee shift, so the leading device of the row's own splice is neither named nor filed. Gloss parity fails in the same place, and by the row's own cut rather than the translation's: the English quotation begins after the frame, though the other witness renders it in that same verse, “Yahweh of Armies says,” (web:Jer.23.16), so gloss extent falls short of splice extent. Naming the mouth is substantive here, not pedantic: the tsevaot form of the messenger formula stands in 50 verses (sweep: 50 verses, MT keys), 21 of them verse-initial, and that verse-initial set holds both oshb:Jer.23.16, where the mouth is the divine speaker's reported by the prophet, and oshb:Jer.28.2, where the identical shape is in a false prophet's mouth. The self-inconsistency is real as filed: strongest_rejected_alternative excuses the following seam as opening even without a formal imperative or koh-amar marker, while the row's own opening verse carries one unnamed. One finding beyond the challenge: a paseq seg stands at oshb:Jer.23.19 inside the span (count-only, WLC single-witness) and is undisclosed, alongside the parashah and ketiv/qere disclosures device_notes does carry correctly (petuchah at 23:15 before the span, setumah at 23:18 and 23:22, the span's one variant note at 23:18 consulted and not spliced). The seam at 23:15|23:16 is not in doubt - on the bytes it is better warranted than the row claims.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: re-describe the opener as the verse-initial messenger frame at oshb:Jer.23.16 with the imperative following it, name the mouth as the divine speaker's reported by the prophet, and extend the English gloss to cover the whole spliced run so gloss extent equals splice extent. (2) observed_substrate_signals: add speech_formula.koh_amar; if the messenger frame is recorded as the leading device rather than a co-signal, treat strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence as dependent fields and re-check them in the same edit. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut so it no longer rests on the absence of a marker the row's own opening verse carries. (4) device_notes: add the one paseq seg at oshb:Jer.23.19 (count-only, single-witness, no position claim). (5) Span unchanged. Tests the cure must pass: gloss extent equals splice extent on every spliced run; every device standing inside a splice appears in the signal list; a span-relevant disclosure sweep over Jer.23.16-Jer.23.22 names parashah, ketiv/qere and paseq; and the rejected alternative no longer cites the absence of a device the row itself splices - the check the original failed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unit's defining device - the burden/oracle wordplay supplying the literature type and the whole cohesion argument - is asserted in English only with no pointed splice, the English witness quoted never carries the burden sense at all, and the byte-level pun closing the unit at 23:39 goes unengaged.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on all three arms, and the splice arm is sharper than filed. The opening splice ends at לֵאמֹ֔ר (oshb:Jer.23.33, byte tier), immediately before the question phrase that carries the noun twice in that same verse: מַה מַשָּׂ֖א יְהוָ֑ה and אֶת מַה מַשָּׂ֔א (oshb:Jer.23.33, byte tier). The quoted English cannot supply the double sense - across web:Jer.23.33-Jer.23.40 that witness renders the noun as the message word 8 times and the burden word 0 times - so a boundary-relevant claim about a two-sense Hebrew noun rests on no quoted evidence, where the engagement class makes a pointed splice with its tier mandatory. The token is hazardous in the direction left undisclosed: the bare noun stands in 7 verses (sweep: 7 verses, MT keys), 4 of them in the sabbath-load material of ch 17 and 3 inside this span, because both forms at oshb:Jer.23.36 are prefixed and invisible to a bare-token sweep. The closing resolution is byte-real and unengaged: oshb:Jer.23.39 reads וְנָשִׁ֥יתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם נָשֹׁ֑א (byte tier), whose infinitive absolute carries the same consonantal skeleton as the noun the unit turns on and stands as a bare token in 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys), so the sentence described only as one of forgetting is where the wordplay resolves at byte level. The continuity claim on 23:38 is true but unevidenced and unfiled: oshb:Jer.23.38 does carry לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier), the divine speaker's own mouth with no tsevaot in that verse, yet no form of it is quoted and observed_substrate_signals records only the discourse imperative and a scene shift. Not in dispute and correctly handled: unit_type stays inside the closed vocabulary with the wordplay kept out of it, the one parashah mark in the span is cited correctly under its type, and no ketiv/qere note or paseq seg falls in Jer.23.33-Jer.23.40. The span itself is not challenged.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: splice both occurrences of the noun from oshb:Jer.23.33 at byte tier with the ref and tier named, and state the double sense as a claim about the Hebrew, adding that the quoted English witness renders the noun with a single word throughout the span (sweep: 8 occurrences of the message word and 0 of the burden word over web:Jer.23.33-Jer.23.40) so the double sense is not taken from the English. (2) Splice the frame from oshb:Jer.23.38 at byte tier naming the mouth, and add speech_formula.koh_amar to observed_substrate_signals. (3) Either engage the closing resolution at oshb:Jer.23.39 with its pointed splice, its skeleton relation to the noun and its digit (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys), or drop the claim that the unit closes on the wordplay's own sentence. (4) Wherever the bare-token digit is used, name the swept object and disclose the two prefixed forms at oshb:Jer.23.36 that a bare-token sweep does not see. (5) Span, unit_type and confidence unchanged. Tests the cure must pass: every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim carries a pointed splice bound to its cited ref that re-collates at byte tier with no normalization required; every device argued in prose appears in the signal list; and every digit names its swept object and unit - the tests the original claim never faced.
